utility_name: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
incentive_structure: rate discount / TOU pricing
on_peak_window: Weekdays High Peak 1-5pm; Low Peak 10am-1pm & 5-8pm; Base 8pm-10am weekdays + all Sat/Sun
peak_offpeak_rates: High Peak > Low Peak > Base (three-tier TOU); rates set by Electric Rate Ordinance, not published on program page

utility_name: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
incentive_structure: one-time enrollment card + annual participation incentive
incentive_value_usd: $55 enroll (one-time); $40/yr at 25-75% event participation; $90/yr at >75% participation
event_limits: up to 30 events/season, 4 hr max, Jun 1-Oct 31 2026, 1-10pm window, holidays excluded

utility_name: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
incentive_structure: retail-rate netting (not subject to CPUC NEM 3.0)
tariff_schedule: NEM Guidelines (LADWP, not a CPUC tariff)
export_compensation: 1:1 retail-rate net metering; LADWP is not bound by CPUC NEM 3.0 avoided-cost export decisions since it is a municipal utility governed by LA City Council/Board of Water and Power Commissioners

utility_name: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
program_name: Self-Generation Incentive Program (SGIP) - Residential Solar and Storage Equity (RSSE)
incentive_structure: upfront rebate, income-qualified pathway only
event_limits: first-come first-served; $32M additional funding announced Aug 2025

incentive_structure: rate discount / TOU pricing
incentive_value_usd: Summer (as of ~2026): peak ~37.65 c/kWh; mid-peak ~21.39 c/kWh; off-peak ~15.50 c/kWh (per third-party report, not directly confirmed on primary page)
on_peak_window: Weekdays 5-8pm peak; all other hours + all weekends/holidays off-peak
peak_offpeak_rates: peak ~37.65c / mid ~21.39c / off ~15.50c per kWh (summer, third-party-reported)

program_name: Solar and Storage Rate (SSR) - Excess Electricity Compensation
incentive_structure: flat per-kWh export credit
event_limits: reviewed every 4 years, capped at +/-30% per cycle
export_compensation: flat 9.6 c/kWh any time of day/season, not CPUC NEM 3.0; legacy NEM customers (pre 3/1/2022) may stay on old NEM through 12/31/2030 with 5.5c/kWh avoided-cost true-up or rollover option

incentive_structure: upfront $/kWh enrollment incentive + ongoing quarterly incentive (Tesla only)
incentive_value_usd: $500/kWh up to $10,000 (projects interconnected by 9/22/2026, enrolled by 12/31/2026); $300/kWh up to $6,000 thereafter; Tesla quarterly: $110 (1 battery)/$220 (2)/$330 (3+)
event_limits: must enroll within 90 days of Permission to Operate; 20% reserve maintained for backup power

incentive_structure: per-event bill credit
event_limits: cycling 30-60 min/hr, up to ~2 hrs per event, events rare (multi-year gaps); not currently installing new devices

program_name: Residential - Time-of-Use Electric Vehicle Option (Pilot Program)
incentive_structure: TOU rate discount for EV charging
retail-rate netting (own tariff, not subject to CPUC NEM 3.0)
event_limits: systems >1MW subject to capacity charge and forfeit excess generation credits
export_compensation: 1:1 retail-rate netting under MID's own NEM2 tariff; MID is not subject to CPUC NEM 3.0 since it is a POU; legacy NEM1 tariff also on file

incentive_structure: enrollment bill credit + season-end participation credit
event_limits: event season May 1-Oct 31; events typically weekdays 12pm-9pm, 1-4 degree adjustment, up to 4 hrs; forfeits participation incentive after opting out of >2 events

incentive_structure: monthly on/off-peak netting + Short Run Marginal Cost true-up for excess
incentive_value_usd: 2024 avg cost of power (SRMC) ~$0.0786/kWh (used for annual excess-generation true-up)
event_limits: system sizes not limited to load at this time; TID reserves right to study/limit interconnection
export_compensation: monthly net on-peak/off-peak energy netting; net annual excess generation credited at TID's published Short Run Marginal Cost, not a 1:1 retail rate and not CPUC NEM 3.0; legacy RNT (residential net metering, true 1:1) closed to new accounts

incentive_structure: rate discount / TOU pricing
on_peak_window: May-Oct: weekdays 4-9pm on-peak; winter on-peak hours differ; weekends/holidays off-peak all day year-round

incentive_structure: variable per-kWh export credit pegged to IID's wholesale solar procurement cost
incentive_value_usd: 6.98 cents/kWh (variable, adjusted as IID's lowest wholesale solar contract cost changes)
event_limits: no participation cap (cap eliminated in 2016 policy change)
export_compensation: monthly netting of consumption vs. generation at customer's load; excess/overgeneration paid at IID's wholesale solar procurement rate (6.98c/kWh), NOT retail 1:1 net metering; IID is a POU governed by its own elected board, not CPUC, so NEM 3.0 does not apply; legacy Net Energy Metering program is closed/fully subscribed and not available to new customers

incentive_structure: enrollment bill credit + per-kWh event performance credit
incentive_value_usd: up to $30 enrollment bill credit; $1.00/kWh reduced during event hours, up to $100/fiscal year
event_limits: non-holiday weekdays, up to 3 hrs/event, 1 event/day, max 10 events/yr; requires interval smart meter
stackable_with: Battery Storage Rebate (requires MyPower + TOU enrollment)

incentive_structure: upfront rebate
event_limits: min 5kWh capacity, UL certified; requires 12-month enrollment in TOU rate + myPower Savings Program

incentive_structure: retail credit netting transitioning to wholesale-based rate under NEM 2.0
event_limits: retail NEM offered up to 5% (30MW) of peak aggregate load, cap met in 2019; NEM1 customers grandfathered unless system expanded
export_compensation: Anaheim not subject to CPUC NEM 3.0 since it is a municipal POU; NEM 2.0 uses wholesale-based (non-retail) export rate vs NEM1's full retail kWh-for-kWh credit; legacy NEM1 customers grandfathered

incentive_structure: rate discount / TOU pricing
event_limits: capped at 500 total customers; closed to new enrollment once cap reached
peak_offpeak_rates: on-peak/mid-peak/off-peak periods defined in tariff (not itemized on program page)

incentive_structure: Avoided Cost of Energy x Time-of-Delivery factor, per-kWh export credit
event_limits: system size up to 150% of historic annual consumption
export_compensation: export credited at RPU's Avoided Cost of Energy adjusted by a Time-of-Delivery factor for the export hour, NOT 1:1 retail net metering and NOT CPUC NEM 3.0 (RPU is a municipal utility, CPUC does not set its solar rules); solar customers placed on DTOU rate; older NEM agreements generally grandfathered

incentive_structure: upfront $/kWh rebate
incentive_value_usd: $500/kWh, up to $10,000/project (standard); $850/kWh up to $17,000 for SHARE-qualified low-income customers
event_limits: $5M program budget; retroactive to systems installed on/after 7/1/2026; requires enrollment in a residential TOU rate

utility_name: Silicon Valley Power (City of Santa Clara)
incentive_structure: rate discount / TOU pricing
event_limits: customer responsible for installed cost of TOU meter
on_peak_window: Peak: Mon-Sat (excl. holidays) starting 6:00am; Off-Peak: all other hours

utility_name: Silicon Valley Power (City of Santa Clara)
incentive_structure: annual netting with Generation Buy-back rate true-up for net export
event_limits: SVP has not reached the 5% aggregate peak load threshold under Public Utilities Code 2827 (own tariff not CPUC-set for POUs)
export_compensation: annual net metering true-up; net excess generation purchased at SVP's Generation Buy-back rate (value not published on program page); SVP is not governed by CPUC NEM 3.0 as a municipal POU

utility_name: Silicon Valley Power (City of Santa Clara)
incentive_structure: upfront $/Wh rebate + income-qualified bonus
incentive_value_usd: $0.15/Wh up to $2,700 base; +$2,000 bonus for Financial Rate Assistance Program enrollees; +$2,000 more for LIHEAP-qualified customers; up to $6,700 total for eligible customers
event_limits: battery must be integrated with PV system, min 3kWh capacity, purchased/installed after 7/1/2024

incentive_structure: rate discount / TOU pricing
incentive_value_usd: High season (Jul-Oct): Base $0.2280/kWh, Peak $0.6839/kWh; Low season (Nov-Jun): Base $0.1901/kWh, Peak $0.5700/kWh; $0.75/meter/day customer charge
on_peak_window: High season peak: weekdays 2-8pm; Low season peak: weekdays 12-9pm; Base = all other hours incl. weekends/holidays
peak_offpeak_rates: High season: base $0.2280 / peak $0.6839 per kWh; Low season: base $0.1901 / peak $0.5700 per kWh

incentive_structure: enrollment + annual anniversary bill credit via prepaid debit card
incentive_value_usd: $50 enrollment + $50/yr on enrollment anniversary (residential); commercial up to $250/event
event_limits: up to 15 events/yr; residential customers may opt out of up to 2 events without losing incentive; designed for up to 10MW controllable demand by 2024

program_name: L-1-D / L-1-E Customer-Owned Generation (Net Energy Metering)
incentive_structure: retail-rate netting under own municipal NEM tariff (not CPUC NEM 3.0)
event_limits: first-come-first-served until total generating capacity exceeds 5% of GWP's aggregate customer peak demand; GWP no longer offers solar incentives but keeps NEM available; L-1-E TOU solar rate not currently offered
export_compensation: excess generation earns a bill credit under GWP's own NEM program; GWP is a municipal POU not governed by CPUC NEM 3.0 decisions
